sources.title: Balkrishna Doshi (Q380449), verified live via the Wikidata API: English label 'Balkrishna Doshi', description 'Indian architect (1927-2023)', instance of human, born 26 August 1927 in Pune, died 24 January 2023 in Ahmedabad, citizenship British Raj and India, occupations architect, urban planner and teacher. No Korean label. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

The Pritzker Architecture Prize, 'Balkrishna Doshi' laureate biography, 2018 announcement and jury citation (read in full). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: first Indian laureate; worked with Le Corbusier in Paris from 1951 and supervised his Ahmedabad buildings, then with Louis Kahn on the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad from 1962; founded his practice Vastushilpa in 1956 and the Vastushilpa Foundation in 1978; founder and director of the School of Architecture and Planning (now CEPT University); his own studio Sangath, the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, the Tagore Memorial Hall, Institute of Indology and the Aranya Low Cost Housing at Indore (Aga Khan Award 1993-95); a 1954 pledge to house 'the lowest class' properly. Award-body copy that quotes his own words; admiring and partly self-reported.

William J. R. Curtis, 'Balkrishna Doshi obituary', The Guardian, 13 February 2023 (read as the extract reproduced by ADA Magazine and Arquitectura Viva; the full Guardian page could not be retrieved). By the author of the standard monograph on Doshi: adaptation of principles from Le Corbusier and Kahn to Indian climate and culture; the half-buried vaulted studio Sangath; the low-cost ATIRA housing at Ahmedabad (1959) and Aranya at Indore, which provided a core of basic amenities and allowed self-built additions; his attempts to learn from slums' social organisation. A monographer's obituary, admiring but analytical.

Sean Anderson, 'Tribute: Balkrishna Doshi (1927-2023)', Architectural Record, 25 January 2023 (read in full). A personal remembrance by a former CEPT teacher: Doshi as storyteller, his years in Le Corbusier's atelier and on Chandigarh, his work with Kahn on the IIM Ahmedabad, the formation of the Institute of Indology and CEPT, Sangath, the 1982-89 Aranya housing, and the Amdavad ni Gufa gallery made with the artist M. F. Husain. Warm and anecdotal, written by an acquaintance.

Vikram Bhatt, 'Balkrishna Doshi's Aranya', Canadian Centre for Architecture, May 2018 (read in full). Account by a McGill researcher who documented the project: Doshi chose to develop Aranya through the Vastushilpa Foundation with the McGill Minimum Cost Housing Group after a study of Indore's informal settlements; the sites-and-services approach with plots, service cores and incremental building; 65 percent of 6,500 plots for lower-income households; growth from a planned 70,000 to about 80,000 residents; earlier company-town and ATIRA housing. Institutional archive essay published for the Pritzker announcement, admiring.

Rahul Srivastava, 'Aranya: A story of incremental development', urbz, 8 August 2011 (read in full). COUNTER-VOICE from an urban-research collective after a site visit: Aranya was a World Bank-supported sites-and-services scheme; many of Doshi's initial intentions and innovations did not survive implementation; many plots passed to buyers other than the intended households and some larger plots were bought as speculation; the town centre was left undeveloped; low-income residents are now a minority; yet the neighbourhood is lively and mixed. Independent of Doshi's practice and critical of the outcome.

Prem Chandavarkar, 'Balkrishna Doshi, the Master Who Never Stopped Learning, With Much Joy and Wonder', The Wire, January 2023 (read in full). Reminiscence by an architect who knew him for four decades: the 1951 move to Paris knowing nobody and speaking no French, his early change of course away from Le Corbusier's idiom, his pocket notebook and attentive note-taking at lectures, climbing a wall and a water tower to see a site, sitting in children's chairs to understand a school, and his acceptance of dinner invitations from young architects. A friend's and mentee's account, admiring and anecdotal.

Thomson Reuters Foundation, 'Building for India's poor: plant a seed to grow a forest', 28 August 2017 (read in full; published on Eco-Business). Interview at the Royal Academy, London, at age 89: Aranya gave each family a plinth with a connection hub for toilet, kitchen tap and electricity and about 80 model house designs; on his return about 35,000 people lived there in resident-built two- and three-storey homes; he said residents 'invented better than the architects could have'. Partly self-reported in an interview; journalist's framing is favourable.

Martino Stierli, 'In Memoriam: Balkrishna V. Doshi (1927-2023)', post: notes on art in a global context, Museum of Modern Art, 9 June 2023 (read in full). MoMA's chief curator of architecture, who featured Doshi in the 2022 exhibition 'The Project of Independence': his training under Le Corbusier, supervision of the Ahmedabad buildings after 1954, his influence in bringing Louis Kahn to Ahmedabad for the IIM, the founding and design of CEPT, the Institute of Indology, Premabhai Hall and the IIM Bangalore, and the present threat of demolition to parts of the IIM Ahmedabad campus. Curatorial memorial, admiring.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_doshi_pritzker, src_doshi_wire, src_doshi_moma, src_doshi_cca | 1951-1978 | award-body biography, friend's tribute, museum memorial, archive essay] He went to Paris in 1951 to work with Le Corbusier although he knew no one and spoke no French, opened his own practice in 1956, founded the school that became CEPT in the 1960s and the Vastushilpa Foundation in 1978, and, per MoMA, used his influence to bring Louis Kahn to Ahmedabad for the IIM. The Paris story is largely his own account repeated; the institution-founding facts are documented by several sources. SELF-CALIBRATION: lowered from 76 / 0.62 because the opening anecdote is one family and the founding record is shared with partners and patrons.

curiosity.rationale: [src_doshi_wire, src_doshi_cca, src_doshi_archrecord | 1950s-2011 | friend's tribute, archive essay, tribute] A friend records his pocket notebook, copious notes at other people's lectures, climbing a construction wall and a 30-metre tank tower to see a site, and sitting in children's chairs at a new school; the McGill-linked archive essay records a systematic study of Indore's informal settlements before Aranya. CONCENTRATION: lowered from 74 / 0.56 because the vivid instances come from one friend's reminiscence.

collaboration.rationale: [src_doshi_pritzker, src_doshi_cca, src_doshi_archrecord, src_doshi_moma | 1954-1995 | award-body biography, archive essay, tribute, museum memorial] He worked as an associate of Louis Kahn on the IIM Ahmedabad for over a decade, collaborated with the McGill Minimum Cost Housing Group on the Indore studies and Aranya, and made the Amdavad ni Gufa with the painter M. F. Husain; his studio's name, Sangath, means to move together. The sources show many partnerships but say little about how he worked within them, and several credits are shared. SELF-CALIBRATION: lowered from 72 / 0.58 for shared-credit inflation.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_doshi_pritzker, src_doshi_cca, src_doshi_urbz, src_doshi_reuters, src_doshi_curtis | 1954-1989 | award-body biography, archive essay, research-collective article, interview, monographer's obituary] He pledged in 1954 to house the poor properly, designed low-income housing from the 1950s (ATIRA, company towns, Aranya) and ran the Aranya work through his research foundation rather than his practice; the research-collective article confirms the project reached lively, mixed neighbourhoods but also that many plots went to others and low-income residents are now a minority. CONCENTRATION: lowered from 76 / 0.60 because the stated motive is his own and the supporting institutional texts share one source; the outcomes were partial.

leadership_drive.rationale: [src_doshi_pritzker, src_doshi_moma, src_doshi_archrecord | 1956-2012 | award-body biography, museum memorial, tribute] He founded and directed the school of architecture and planning that became CEPT (1966-2012 in the Pritzker account), founded his own firm with a growing partner group and the Vastushilpa Foundation, and served on selection committees. The sources describe institutions he founded but little about how he led people, and the credit is shared with colleagues. SELF-CALIBRATION: lowered from 66 / 0.52 and relabelled inference.

belief_updating.rationale: [src_doshi_wire, src_doshi_pritzker | 1960s-1980s | friend's tribute, award-body biography] A friend describes him as one of the first to move away from the Le Corbusier-derived exposed-concrete idiom of the Institute of Indology and Tagore Memorial Hall toward space and inhabitation, and the jury says his early work was influenced by Le Corbusier and Kahn and then moved beyond it. CONCENTRATION: lowered from 64 / 0.50 and relabelled inference because the shift is described by one commentator and the jury's summary.

cross_domain_range.rationale: [src_doshi_pritzker, src_doshi_archrecord, src_doshi_cca | 1956-1995 | award-body biography, tribute, archive essay] Architecture, urban planning, teaching, a research foundation and a built collaboration with an artist (the Gufa with Husain) are all documented. Most of it lies inside the built environment, which keeps the score moderate.

risk_tolerance.rationale: [src_doshi_wire, src_doshi_cca, src_doshi_urbz | 1951-1989 | friend's tribute, archive essay, research-collective article] The unplanned move to Paris and the choice to make Aranya an open framework that residents would build themselves were both exposed to failure; the research-collective article records that part of the original intention did not survive and that the plots drifted away from the intended households. The sources do not say how he weighed the risks.

resourcefulness.rationale: [src_doshi_cca, src_doshi_reuters, src_doshi_curtis | 1956-1989 | archive essay, interview, monographer's obituary] Facing scarce steel and cement he built the ATIRA housing with load-bearing brick and vaults, and at Aranya he supplied each family only a plinth with a service hub and demonstration designs so that residents could build with local materials. CONCENTRATION: lowered from 64 / 0.50 and relabelled inference because the archive essay and the interview rest on the same project account.

portrait.source: Photograph of Balkrishna Doshi at the Indian Institute of Architects National Convention held in Chennai in December 2013 (Commons description: 'held at Chennai Trade Centre'; a convention attendee's blog places the three-day convention at the Chennai Convention Center and records Doshi's keynote), taken by Sanyam Bahga on 27 December 2013 with a Nikon D60 (EXIF) and uploaded by him to Wikimedia Commons as his own work. The Commons file is a 825 x 1032 pixel crop of the 3872 x 2592 camera frame; used as is, re-encoded only, not resized and not upscaled.

provenance.notes: portrait_preflight: STRONG (Stage B) / lead SURVIVED with one correction. Lead: Commons 'Balkrishna Doshi.JPG' by Sanyam Bahga (own work, CC BY-SA 3.0, 2013-12-27, Nikon D60). Re-verified: Commons record read through the API (author Sanyambahga, own work, licence CC BY-SA 3.0, attribution required, 825 x 1032, EXIF Nikon D60 and an original frame of 3872 x 2592 are preserved in the file); the original download matches. CORRECTION to the preflight: the preflight reported an in-image caption 'B.V Doshi', but the Commons file shows no lettering at all, so sitter identity rests on the uploader's description ('Balkrishna Doshi at IIA National Convention 2013'), a convention attendee's blog that records Doshi's keynote at that December 2013 Chennai convention, and a visual match with widely published pictures of him (distinctive swept-back grey hair and round dark glasses); no second lettering or group-order evidence exists, so this is the portrait's main caveat. No external holder record exists (own-work upload). The uploader's identity as the photographer was not independently verified beyond the Commons record and EXIF. The attendee blog names the venue as the Chennai Convention Center whereas the Commons description says Chennai Trade Centre; the discrepancy does not affect identity and the file description is quoted as Commons gives it. A second free route (Gujarat Vishw Kosh Trust 2017 award photograph, CC BY-SA 4.0, 1200 x 800) could not be downloaded (Wikimedia rate limit) and was not used. Rights: CC BY-SA 3.0 requires visible attribution to Sanyam Bahga and a share-alike notice; precedent exists in the roster (e.g. Ada Yonath). Kind likeness (photograph from life, age 86). No upscaling. ATTRIBUTION: attributable (extensive public record; building credits are shared and scored only as conduct). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Pritzker Prize biography and jury citation (https://www.pritzkerprize.com/laureates/balkrishna-doshi). READ (8 sources besides Wikidata): Pritzker page (full); Curtis obituary extract (partial; the full Guardian page was not retrievable); Architectural Record tribute (full); CCA Aranya essay (full); urbz article (full); The Wire tribute (full); Thomson Reuters interview (full); MoMA memorial (full). Also read and not cited: Wallpaper interview, Dezeen and The Federal obituaries, The Art Newspaper note, Docomomo note. Wikipedia not used. Not opened: Doshi's memoir Paths Uncharted, Curtis's monograph, the McGill post-occupancy report (fetched as an HTML shell), the Aga Khan jury report. PERSPECTIVES: (1) award-body jury citation (partly his own words); (2) monographer's obituary; (3) McGill-linked archive essay on Aranya; (4) independent urban-research counter-voice on Aranya outcomes (urbz); (5) friend and mentee tribute; (6) museum curator memorial; (7) journalist interview. NON-SELF BEHAVIOURAL SOURCES: urbz, The Wire, CCA, Architectural Record, MoMA, Curtis; the Pritzker page and the Reuters interview contain his own statements. CONTRADICTIONS AND LIMITS: the date of founding of the CEPT school differs by source (1962 in MoMA and Wallpaper, 1966 in the Pritzker biography and Dezeen) so cards say 'in the 1960s'; Aranya's resident count differs (about 60,000, 80,000 or 35,000 in 2017) and is stated with attribution; the urbz article reports that many original design intentions and the low-income target group were not preserved, which tempers the housing story; credit on the IIM Ahmedabad is shared with Louis Kahn and Anant Raje. ZERO POLITICS: primary identity is architect, educator and institution builder; the prime minister's tribute and national honours are not used as evidence. MAJOR ACHIEVEMENT GATE (pass): see handback. SELF-CALIBRATION: initial 9 rows; concentration lowered 4 (curiosity, impact motivation, belief updating, resourcefulness); self-calibration lowered 3 more (proactive agency, collaboration, leadership drive); none raised. Eligibility: fewer than 18 scored attributes by design; sparse profile is valid.
